security_audit.summary: The confirmed findings are manual npx installation commands and belt CLI examples that can run external commands or send image data to remote services. Many other static hits are Markdown fence delimiters or inline documentation links, and no prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the smallest belt subcommands needed, or require confirmation before login, install, store, and upload actions.
Pin trusted versions for npx skill installation guidance and clearly label each command as a manual setup step.
Tell users that prompts and referenced images may be sent to inference.sh services before running belt app commands.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Belt CLI Permission

content.value_statement: Product teams need polished images for listings, ads, and catalogs without a full studio shoot. This skill provides prompt patterns for packshots, lifestyle scenes, lighting, angles, and complete image sets.
actual_capabilities: Provides prompt patterns for hero shots, packshots, lifestyle scenes, scale shots, detail shots, and collection images.
Explains product-friendly camera angles such as eye level, overhead, low angle, and three-quarter view.
Lists lighting styles, shadow types, backgrounds, and composition rules for commercial product images.
Outlines a 7 to 9 image e-commerce listing sequence with roles for each image.
Gives category-specific guidance for food, jewelry, electronics, cosmetics, and apparel.
Shows belt CLI examples for generation, image editing, and upscaling workflows.
limitations: Requires access to the belt CLI and supported remote image generation services.
Does not verify marketplace policy compliance for every platform or product category.
Cannot guarantee generated images match the exact physical product without careful review.
May require user approval before uploading private product images to remote services.

use_cases.title: Launch Listing Images
use_cases.description: Create a structured set of hero, lifestyle, scale, detail, and packaging images for a new product page.

use_cases.title: Improve Brand Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Develop consistent product image prompts that match a campaign mood, lighting style, and background family.

use_cases.title: Prototype Catalog Concepts
use_cases.description: Test product angles, props, and category conventions before scheduling a studio shoot or vendor brief.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Packshot
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a clean product listing image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a packshot prompt for [product]. Use a pure white background, even studio light, sharp focus, and no props.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Lifestyle Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for showing product context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a lifestyle product photography prompt for [product] used by [customer]. Include setting, props, lighting, mood, and camera angle.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Listing Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for an e-commerce image sequence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a 7 image product listing set for [product]. Include hero, lifestyle, scale, detail, alternate angle, packaging, and feature callout images.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Category Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for category-specific art direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite these product image prompts for [category]. Match category conventions for lighting, surface, props, shadows, angle, and resolution.

output_examples.input: A skincare founder needs a marketplace-ready hero image for a serum bottle.
output_examples.output: A packshot brief with pure white background, centered bottle, soft even light, readable label detail, and clean shadow control.

output_examples.input: An electronics team needs lifestyle images for a portable speaker.
output_examples.output: A prompt plan with poolside context, warm natural light, simple props, scale reference, and a matching close-up detail shot.

output_examples.input: A catalog manager needs a full image set for a leather bag.
output_examples.output: A sequence covering hero, model lifestyle, material close-up, scale, alternate angle, packaging, and feature callout images.

best_practices: Start with the required marketplace image type, then choose lighting, angle, background, and shadow style.
Keep packshots simple and reserve props, people, and environments for lifestyle or scale images.
Review generated images for product accuracy, readable labels, trademark issues, and platform requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unrelated props, busy backgrounds, and strong shadows in primary listing images.
Do not use lifestyle prompts when the marketplace requires a pure white primary image.
Do not upload confidential product images to remote tools without user approval.

faq.question: What products does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers common product categories, including food, jewelry, electronics, cosmetics, apparel, accessories, and packaged goods.

faq.question: Can it create Amazon-style listing images?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes packshot guidance for white backgrounds, product size, image order, and common marketplace expectations.

faq.question: Does it replace a professional photo shoot?
faq.answer: No. It helps create concepts and generated assets, but physical accuracy and legal review remain user responsibilities.

faq.question: Does it need external services?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use the belt CLI to call remote image generation, editing, and upscaling services.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing product image?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes image-to-image editing examples for changing backgrounds while preserving the product.

faq.question: How should teams keep image sets consistent?
faq.answer: Use the same lighting family, background style, camera angle logic, and resolution targets across the full set.
